The one real judgment call is how I forbare to come divides. Kept as accepted: ouketi takes forbare, elthon takes the discontinuous I ... to come. The subject is licensed by the Greek verb's person inflection under rule 9, and ouketi is an adverb with no person to license it, so I rides with elthon even though English finiteness sits on forbare; rule 17 refuses finiteness and word order as criteria. Both units stay medium under rule 16.

for a witness is kept whole on martyra. No Greek preposition is expressed for the supplied for to answer to, so rule 67 does not apply and the supplied preposition and determiner are rule 7 helpers; the head is on witness, the word the corpus spends on the martyr- lexeme (rules 17, 66, 91).

Both articles are unrepresented for different reasons: s004 because the ASV writes a bare God (rule 23), s008 because the possessive adjective emen occupies the determiner slot (rules 20, 54). Rule 21 is not in play for s008, since an expressed epi already takes upon under rule 36.
hoti here introduces reported speech the ASV spells with that, so rule 43's unrepresented arm does not reach it.
